title: The Silent Vault of Marlowe Jewelers
story:
Renowned jeweler Victor Marlowe was found dead inside his high‑security vault at precisely 10:23 AM. The vault door was bolted from the inside, the only air vent was sealed, and the alarm recorded no breach. The room showed no sign of forced entry, yet Victor lay on the polished floor with a single, clean stab wound to the heart. 

Four people were present in the building that morning. Marco, Victor’s long‑time assistant, claims he was polishing the display cases in the back office at 10:00 AM and heard nothing. Elena, a rival jeweler who had a heated argument with Victor the night before, says she was in the lobby negotiating a purchase and left the premises at 9:45 AM. Victor’s night‑shift security guard, Victor (the guard), insists he was on his break from 10:00 to 10:30 AM in the staff lounge, checking the CCTV monitors intermittently. Finally, Sofia, Victor’s estranged sister, states she arrived at the building at 10:15 AM to deliver a family heirloom and found the door already locked from the inside.
crimeScene: Marlowe Jewelers’ underground vault – a sealed steel room with a single air vent and an internal lock that can only be engaged from inside.
forensicClue: A faint smear of lemon oil and a single partial fingerprint on the inner side of the vent latch, matching Marco’s left thumb; the vent’s latch can only be opened from the outside with a special tool that Marco keeps for cleaning the display cases.
question: Who is the culprit and how was the locked‑room murder accomplished?
options: Option A (Elena – the rival jeweler, who could have slipped a duplicate key into the vent during her lobby visit)
Option B (Marco – the assistant, who used his cleaning tool to open the vent, entered, killed Victor, and sealed the latch behind him)
Option C (Victor – the security guard, who fabricated his break alibi and disabled the alarm)
Option D (Sofia – the sister, who entered through a hidden service door she claimed to be delivering a heirloom through)
deductionExplanation: The vent latch bore lemon oil, a cleaning agent only Marco uses on the jewelry cases, and his fingerprint was found on the inner side of the latch – a place no one else could reach without opening the vent from outside. The vent can be opened only with the specialized tool Marco keeps in his toolbox, confirming he was the only person capable of accessing the vault without breaking the door. All other suspects have alibis that either place them elsewhere or lack the means to manipulate the vent. Therefore, Marco is indisputably the murderer.
